# Build & Learn — Tutorial Content Workflow V1.3 (2026-10-25)

> **Fourth editorial direction:** Teach people how to complete a real task, with **reproducible instructions** rather than generic tool introductions. This workflow **extends** existing AI productivity / GitHub Skills / monetization posts; it does not create a new account, tool stack or scheduled bot.

## V1.3: Mandatory AI-work productivity OR monetization value gate

**BEFORE writing any tutorial, apply [Tutorial Value and Monetization Gate](TUTORIAL-VALUE-AND-MONETIZATION-GATE.md).** This policy overrides mere tutorial popularity, a GitHub Star count, abstract "AI literacy", or the previous assumption that any generic operating guide is suitable. The reader must perform a **specific repeatable job using an AI or automation technique**, with **A** a credible measurable time/cost/error improvement **or B** a lawful buyer, scoped paid outcome and economic/validation test. If a technical concept is prerequisite to practical AI engineering, name that work path and its falsifiable learning milestone; **do not invent future income**.

**Two distinct proof tracks:** `EFFICIENCY_WORKFLOW` must measure original human time vs AI-assisted execution, review and rework; `BUILD_TO_SELL` must identify buyer, deliverables, acquisition, ongoing support, pricing hypothesis and a permissioned pilot. `CREATOR_TECH_OPS` and `TECHNICAL_ENABLER` need equivalent precise results. Unknown outcomes are `UNMEASURED`, not 0.

**Source review:** [Four benchmark X articles and credibility decisions](TUTORIAL-FOUR-X-REFERENCE-AUDIT-2026-10-25.md): @noahduck283 (real work scenario + gateway + 7 pitfalls), @HytidelLegend (complete business lifecycle; reject deceptive sales methods), @AI_Jasonyu (detailed payout onboarding but **obsolete** since old Creator Revenue Sharing ended Sep 7 2026), @Zesee (creator pipeline and first-person earnings; income not independently audited). The articles are editorial references, not ready-to-run scripts or reusable illustrations. **Trust current official platform policy, explicit user authorization and source licenses above peer anecdotes.**

**Hard-stop safety:** No fake orders, fake reviews/SKUs, fabricated titles/credentials, impersonation, KYC/payment/tax or region misrepresentation, stolen client data or license violations. Human approval before autonomous file changes, payments or publication. CC BY-NC assets (e.g. dbskill) are not approved for commercial redistribution without permission.

**Full tutorial structure:** outcome demo (genuinely observed or labeled concept) → who/why → setup/budget/permissions → actual architecture/steps → explicit verification → 3 realistic pitfalls & recoveries → reader-owned artifact → measured efficiency or buyer-pilot plan → upkeep. For broad topics 8–15 sections are a useful editorial target. For narrow labs use a narrow honest title. **All X assets still require real matching 16:9 PNG/JPG + ALT, not an SVG-only or text-only delivery.**

## V1.2: Longform-first gate

The original #006 causal-mask mini lab was actually tested, but did NOT fulfill the broad brief “How to Learn LLMs from GitHub”. The user-preferred [October 23 task-first X Article](https://x.com/goan999999/status/2113525221374488901) uses an end-to-end 13-section reader journey. Borrow the educational **structure**, not its prose or screenshots.

For end-to-end how-to topics, create a full 8–15 section task-driven lesson (editorial target) **before** X copy. Cover problem, sources, eligibility and dependencies, steps, expected checks, errors, learner-owned artifact, advanced roadmap and honest work/business application. **Every main section includes an action and checkpoint.** Tested toy script stays a subsection. Clearly mark which steps actually passed tests versus sourced UI instructions that were not independently performed. A private internal README is not a public original tutorial link. The cover image must express the entire journey, not the narrow sub-experiment. Reference: [Editorial audit](TUTORIAL-LONGFORM-EDITORIAL-REVIEW.md), [#007 revised post](../posts/2026-10-25-007-github-llm-longform.md).

## Scope and editorial promise

**Positioning:** "One useful outcome, real steps, verifiable checkpoints, no hidden prerequisites." Tutorials may cover (i) running X/Xiaohongshu creator accounts; (ii) learning and building LLMs from public GitHub projects; (iii) making an AI media workflow; (iv) building a clearly specified self-hosted service/network node; (v) automation, engineering and monetizable delivery. **Each must help a defined reader become able to do something independently.** No untested "full-course in one click" or fake ROI.

**Target audience:** AI learners, indie builders, self-media operators, small-business implementers; English X distribution remains the immediate channel. Chinese platform versions are optional derivatives, not a reason to dilute the X account with unrelated lifestyle topics.

**Cadence at V0:** **1 genuinely reproduced tutorial package per week** as a planning hypothesis, plus ordinary daily posts. A full tutorial can take longer than a daily X post; if replication is pending, publish neither a false "step-by-step tested" label nor an unproven tutorial. All X tutorial teasers still require a real matched 16:9 PNG/JPG and English ALT per [hard gate](POST-IMAGE-DELIVERY-GATE.md).

## Discover → Verify → Teach → Distribute → Maintain

### Stage 1 — Learner's task / demand
1. Define **audience + exact job + minimum observable result**, e.g. "LLM beginner can run one inference and explain cost", not "master AI in a day".
2. Gather candidate pain points from X discussion/search, YouTube audience Trends/comments and official videos, Xiaohongshu search suggestions/笔记灵感, Bilibili questions, GitHub Discussions/Issues, official docs. Treat popularity as *demand signal*, not proof.
3. Check overlap with previous posts and [tutorial queue](../templates/tutorial-candidates.csv); record origin URL, snapshot/source provenance, search phrase, beginner/intermediate level, version risk and rights.

### Stage 2 — Resource aggregation: cite original sources, never scrape blindly
1. **Priority A — primary:** official product docs and help centers, actual GitHub repo README/lesson/Release/source code, maintainer examples, platform policy.
2. **Priority B — curricula:** Microsoft Learn/Generative-AI-for-Beginners, Datawhale diy-llm/self-llm, LangChain Academy, Quarto samples, structured chapter-based learning content. Inspect actual prerequisites and runnable parts.
3. **Priority C — community needs:** YouTube/X/Xiaohongshu/Bilibili discussions and error reports. Reproducibility/answers must still be validated with A sources.
4. **Feeds/watchlists:** GitHub Watch Releases & Discussions + official RSS + saved YouTube playlists + manually curated X lists/bookmarks. [RSSHub](https://github.com/DIYgod/RSSHub), [Folo](https://github.com/RSSNext/Folo), [changedetection.io](https://github.com/dgtlmoon/changedetection.io) are **future options**. Don't connect accounts, crawl sites against terms, harvest private content or trigger paid tools by default.
5. Maintain [SOURCE REGISTER](TUTORIAL-SOURCES-2026-10-25.md) + [tutorial-candidates.csv](../templates/tutorial-candidates.csv). Record canonical URL, checked date, version/commit, author, license/attribution, factual trust, access restrictions, status. **Do not store entire copied creator tutorials or video transcripts.**

### Stage 3 — Select viable tutorials
Use an **editorial** 0–5 assessment per dimension: learner demand, narrow outcome clarity, credible source/rights, ability to reproduce on documented environment, value to time/cost/earning goal, manageable maintenance/permissions. /30 recommendation ≥24 AND **primary source + feasible reproduction** mandatory. Does not estimate platform virality.

Reject when: setup depends on prohibited access, unspecified "free" API subscriptions, unlicensed republishing, unclear machine/OS, unresolved privacy/secret handling, financial or productivity claims without evidence, or "one click" instructions that actually skip critical steps. **Self-built 节点** must first state what "node" means (cloud compute/VPS, n8n workflow node, home networking/VPN, blockchain node, etc.) and jurisdiction/provider/acceptable use, then choose official docs. No generic copy-pasted install commands under an ambiguous label.

### Stage 4 — Make a reproducible source lesson (GitHub first)
Create a runbook based on [TUTORIAL-RUNBOOK.md](../templates/TUTORIAL-RUNBOOK.md) with:
1. Goal/demo result (a screenshot, command output, file and check).
2. Reader level, prerequisites, **OS, runtime, dependency versions, GPU/CPU requirements, access, API and likely costs**; declare available verified free alternative if any.
3. Exact source repositories with **full names + permalinks to versions/paths**, license + author, and distinction between upstream procedure and original adaptation.
4. Numbered **input → action/command → expected output → verification** for every important step; code fences are copy/paste-ready and all tokens/IDs use safe placeholders.
5. A **failure branch** for 2–3 common errors, diagnosis, fixes, rollback/recovery, security/privacy pitfalls; no fabricated test logs.
6. Acceptance test a second reader can run, plus bounded demo artifact/sample data with rights checks.
7. Reproduction log with date, environment, exact tested revision, results and evidence; when not run mark `REPRO_PENDING` and **do not advertise a complete verified hands-on tutorial**.

Version drift is a feature, not an embarrassment: link exact tested versions and review critical guides when dependencies change.

### Stage 5 — Two content layers, one knowledge asset
- **Layer A: full tutorial** in this repository under `tutorials/<slug>/README.md` plus small sanitized screenshots, working sample commands/code, troubleshooting, citations and change history. **This is the canonical teaching asset.**
- **Layer B: X discovery asset**: English one-post hook + one specific result, or at most 3 Thread posts when necessary. Every X publish unit gets a matching **actual X-uploadable PNG/JPG + ALT**; use a real result/terminal screenshot (secrets removed) or a clean steps schematic exported to PNG. Include canonical tutorial URL where space permits.
- **Optional platform derivatives:** Xiaohongshu practical cover + step-by-step carousel + caveats; YouTube/Bilibili real screen-capture segmented by chapters; blog/documentation article for searchers. Translate/adapt the *same verified procedure*, do not claim all outputs have been tested per platform.
- Do not manufacture fake terminal output or claim a GitHub README summary was personally reproduced. Don't let a strong hook replace any missing tutorial step.

### Stage 6 — Review
Use [Tutorial Card](../templates/TUTORIAL-CARD.md) AND [X image delivery gate](POST-IMAGE-DELIVERY-GATE.md). **Two separate approvals:** `lesson_repro_verified` and `x_media_ready`. Draft approval requires source, rights, secret scan, successful expected checks and image fidelity. If no rerun, mark `research_only` / `REPRO_PENDING`, not "complete tutorial".

### Stage 7 — Publish
Complete first-party lesson URL → prepared matching English X copy/image/ALT → manual X post → actual X status URL. For 2–3 connected posts, attach a cover image to the first and keep the thread tied to the same lesson. GitHub source/artifact must exist before "Full guide" is promised. No X account authorization is presumed.

### Stage 8 — Measure and update
- X: actual impressions, saves/bookmarks, substantive replies, profile visits or follows when available.
- Learning utility: reproducibility questions, failure rate from voluntary reports, readers who can complete checkpoints, GitHub issues and corrections.
- Cross-platform: Xiaohongshu saves/search queries (only if data actually available); YouTube video retention/chapter drop-offs where available; do not compare unlike metrics as though the same metric.
- Bug/major version change → `needs_revalidation` and edit tutorial, preserve changelog and source commit. **Tutorial upkeep is part of the cost.**

## Four content themes (initial *hypothesis*, not proven ideal)
| Pillar | Initial share | Example |
|---|---:|---|
| Practical Skills / GitHub projects | 30% | One Skill applied to a real task with limits |
| Verified AI / Github improvements | 30% | Specific release with mechanistic change |
| Build-to-Sell reality check | 20% | Buyer, deliverable, measured costs and validation |
| **Build & Learn tutorials** | **20%** | Complete runnable lesson + X copy and matching image |

**Tutorials may overlap an AI Skill or commercial case, but each publication has ONE primary category.** With daily posts, aim to **pilot one full tutorial weekly** and adjust after 4 lessons; percentages are planning targets, not automated publication quotas.

## Concrete multi-platform production schedule

For the source-to-platform transformation, editorial sprint and an **unreproduced GitHub→LLM pilot**, see [Tutorial Platform Packaging](TUTORIAL-PLATFORM-PACKAGING.md). This is guidance for future content derivatives, **not an automatic cross-post implementation**.

## Platform evidence behind this SOP
- [X official article format](https://help.x.com/en/using-x/articles): purpose-driven hook, evidence, formatting, graphics, and linked short posts. Article publishing has eligibility constraints; **GitHub README is default full guide**.
- [X thread procedure](https://help.x.com/en/using-x/create-a-thread): native multi-post composition.
- [YouTube creator topic groups](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/13616340?hl=en) & [Analytics Trends](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/11962757?hl=en): start from topic/learner demand; group formats and evaluate data.
- [YouTube video chapters](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/9884579?hl=en): segment long lessons into named, revisit-friendly steps.
- [Xiaohongshu official learning](https://school.xiaohongshu.com/) & [platform notebook recommendations](https://school.xiaohongshu.com/lesson/normal/af0fe7e97bb0433fac9da5d1df52b07f): searchable topic queries, accurate cover/title, how-to usefulness, quality and notebook analysis. **Some material pertains to merchant notes**, not a universal creator ranking algorithm.
- [Douyin official course](https://school.douyin.com/premium/course/6901561449299050509): account positioning, content creation, data and fan management; not a guaranteed traffic formula.
- [GitHub hands-on tutorials](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/tutorials) and [GitHub Skills education](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/start-your-journey/git-and-github-learning-resources): prerequisites, actions, observable checks and interactive feedback.

**No plugin deployment or X API publishing is part of this addition.**
